newsitem.title: UK: Italian, Spanish debt star in week - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Italian, Spanish debt star in week - Salomon.

text.p: Italian and Spanish bonds were star performers in the latest week, data from Salomon Brothers showed on Friday.
Talk of interest rate cuts drove Italian BTPs 1.20 percent higher in local currency terms, while Spanish bonos gained 1.49 percent.
The Salomon Brothers World Government Bond Index gained 0.38 percent in local currency terms for the week ended April 10.
"Europe finished on a high note, with very bright rays of sunshine coming through on the inflation front," said David Brown, European economist at Bear Stearns International here.
French bonds gained 0.82 percent in francs, while German debt was 0.48 percent higher in marks.
Peripheral European bond markets also benefited from renewed optimism that European economic and monetary union (EMU) will start on time in January 1999.
The dollar bloc sector was the only weak performer in a bullish period for bonds.
Treasuries eased off by 0.06 percent, while Canadian dollar bonds were 0.14 percent lower in local terms. Australian debt, buoyed by market-friendly March employment data, rose by 0.98 percent.
The picture was different in dollar terms, where record highs for the U.S. currency versus the yen led to steep losses in almost all bond markets measured in dollars.
German bonds were down 2.37 percent in dollars, while JGBs slumped by 2.34 percent.
Australian bonds were the only gainers in dollars, rising 1.14 percent. The index as a whole fell by 1.20 percent in dollar terms.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
